title: Successful Microsoft Entra ROPC sign-in
description: Detects a successful Microsoft Entra sign-in that used the resource owner password credentials authentication protocol.

hypothesis.summary: An adversary may use a captured password through the ROPC flow to obtain access without an interactive browser session.
hypothesis.rationale: Microsoft recommends avoiding ROPC because the application handles the user password and explicitly recommends monitoring successful ROPC sign-ins; authorized test automation or a documented legacy workload can still use the protocol.
hypothesis.detection_goal: Identify successful sign-ins whose recorded authentication protocol is ROPC while leaving failed attempts and other authentication protocols unmatched.

triage.summary: Confirm that the application and user are explicitly approved for ROPC, then investigate the source and adjacent authentication activity.
steps: Review the account, application, source IP, authentication requirement, Conditional Access result and correlation identifier.
Confirm a documented ROPC dependency and owner; treat unexpected use by privileged accounts or unfamiliar applications as higher priority.
Inspect nearby failures, risk events, token use and account changes; revoke sessions and reset credentials when compromise is suspected.
false_positives: Approved automated testing or documented legacy applications that still require ROPC

validation.expected_outcome: Match successful ROPC sign-ins; do not match failed ROPC attempts, other protocols, incomplete events or unrelated records.
